GROUND RULES: Contestants who choose to enter the Legacy Steer Roping event must be at least 50 years old at the time of entry closing or a permit member. They must also be entered in the steer roping event at the 101 Wild West Rodeo. To be eligible, the contestant must not have been an NFSR qualifier during the past 3 years. Permit members of all ages are eligible to enter.

Contestants will pay entry fees of $300. Contestants will not compete on any additional steers. The times that are recorded for the contestants' competition runs at the 101 Wild West Rodeo will be used to determine the payoff. Payoff will only include the entry fees for the contestants who entered the Legacy Steer Roping through PROCOM. 6% will be held out of the total amount for the PRCA prior to the payoff. Only the three go-rounds and the average after three go-rounds will be included in the pay-off for the Legacy Steer Roping. There will be no additional added money and since no additional animals will be run, there will be no additional stock charge or PROCOM charge.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. (NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).
STK CONT.: Various

detailLines: Wildwood AB CN NPP
June 13
Wildwood Bronc Bustin'
ARENA: Wildwood AG Grounds
ADDRESS: 5140-50 St.
PERFS: 1 Perf: June 13- 1:00 PM
EVENTS: SB @ $30000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES:
PERMITS: SB
GROUND RULES: May also enter online between May 24 at 8 AM and May 25 at 2 PM.

QUALIFICATIONS: 30 entries. 7 from 2025 CPRA standings. 7 from 2025 PRCA standings. 8 from 2026 CPRA standings as of May 26, 2026. 7 from 2026 PRCA standings as of May 26, 2026 Any remaining positions will be filled based first on 2025 CPRA standings, 2025 PRCA standings, then a random draw of card holders, then semi pro card holders. If there are still remaining open positions, they will be filled by a random draw of permit holders.

FORMAT: One go-round with a top 8 finals. If there are not 8 qualified rides during the long go-round, all remaining positions will be filled by random draw. If 8th place is tied going into the finals, the tie will be broken by the highest marked spur ride from the long go-round. If still tied, the tie will be broken by random draw.
PAY-OFF: 50% of the total purse for the long go-round and 50% for the short go-round. Long go-round will pay 8 places. Short go-round will pay 4 places. There will be no average pay-off.

WALK-UP REPLACEMENT: Contestants who have originally entered and were eligible at time of entry but were drawn out may, in person, check with the rodeo secretary no later than 1 hour prior to the performance to confirm their availability and desire to be an alternate. If selected, by random draw of all walk-ups available, an alternate will assume the competition position of the contestant that he is replacing. In the rough stock, they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned-out stock for the performance and all re-ride stock for that performance.

**If a contestant notifies a turn-out, DR or visible release and is replaced by an alternate, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If the contestant that notified the turnout or visible release is not replaced by an alternate, they will be responsible for the entry fee. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees.**

NOTE: Money won at Xtreme Broncs Events will count towards X-Broncs Standings which will be used for qualifying for the finale in Rapid City. In order for money won in the Wildwood Saddle Bronc competition to count for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo or the 2026 Rookie of the Year standings, during the 2026 season, a contestant must have entered and competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos. Money won at the Wildwood Saddle Bronc competition will not count towards All-Around standings.
STK CONT.: Various

ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information Section of the Business Journal.

ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions on Mon., June 8 between 9 AM and 11 AM. See Rodeo Entry Information section of the business journal.
RIDING EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Fri., June 5 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.

TIMED EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Wed., June 10 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM. Contestants who are placed in the performances will be allowed to trade their second go-round positions with contestants who are placed in other performances. Contestants will not be allowed to trade from a performance to the slack. The rodeo secretary will post the trade deadline in the rodeo office.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes or a re-run is awarded for any other reason during a performance, the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into herd.
TR - Only two loops allowed.

TD, SW, TR FORMAT - Two go-rounds plus a top 12 finals. All contestants will run their first go-round in the slack. The top 50 based on fastest times from the first go-round will be placed in the first 5 performances and the remaining contestants will run their second go-round in reverse order of the first go-round in slack, following the completion of the first go-round. If there are less than 50 qualified times in the first go-round, the remaining available positions in the performances (not to exceed 50) will be filled by the contestants with no qualified times in the first go-round based on the placement order for the second go-round. If ties result in more than 50 to be placed in the performances, a random draw will determine which of the tied contestants will be placed in the performances (will not exceed 50). Placement in the performances will be in accordance with R2.6 of the PRCA Rulebook (pertaining to progressive go-rounds). Contestants who are placed in the performances will not be allowed to trade to the slack. Contestants will be allowed to trade from one performance to a different performance, up to 5 PM the day prior to the 1st performance.

ALL EVENTS - If a contestant who qualifies for the Finals notifies a turn-out, doctors release, or a visible injury release through PROCOM, the constant with the next highest ranking in the average may be contacted by Procom and placed in that available position. Non-notified turn-outs and visible injury releases after the turn-out deadline will not be replaced. If the next highest ranked contestant is not available to accept the position the next highest ranked contestant may be contacted and placed in that position. This procedure will be followed until all positions are filled. The replacement contestant's competition order will be based on his ranking in the average (not on the ranking of the contestant that he is replacing). In riding events, if an animal has already been drawn for a contestant who has turned-out, the replacement contestant will draw an animal from a pool consisting of all animals that have been turned-out (includes DR's and VIR's).
GB - Approved for first slack event in accordance with R4.9.4.

SLACK ORDER - Sunday, June 14 at 7:00 AM: GB (1st go-round), Breakaway (1st Go-round), TD (1st go-round with the exception of approximately 30 contestants that will compete during Monday's slack), Breakaway (2nd go-round), SW (approximately 50% of the 1st go-round. Monday, June 15 at 7:00 AM: TR (1st go-round), TD (finish 1st go-round with about 30 contestants), SW (finish the second half of the 1st go-round), TD (2nd go-round), GB (2nd go-round). Tuesday, June 16 at 8:30 AM: TR (2nd go-round), SW (2nd go-round).
QUALIFICATIONS: BB - 60 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals.
SB - 70 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals.
BR - 80 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals. There may be two sections.
TD, SW, TR - 110 minimum entries.

ALL CONTESTANTS - There will be an extended grace period for those contestants who are entered and meet qualifications to change preferences on Mon., May 18 between 2 and 5 PM (Contestants are not allowed to draw out during the extended grace period).

ALL EVENTS - The "walk-up replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information section of the Business Journal.

RIDING EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Wed., June 10 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.

TIMED EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Mon., June 15 at 4 PM. (Contestants who entered during the "Re-entry" period will not be allowed first go-round trades). All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Must sign a release form at check-in.
ALL CONTESTANTS - All contestants are required to wear PRCA patch while competing.
ALL EVENTS - If contestant notifies a turn-out prior to the "30-hour" deadline for his scheduled competition time, turn-out fines will be waived if and only if he is replaced.

ALL CONTESTANTS - If a contestant who qualifies for the finals notifies a turn-out, doctor's release or visible injury release through PROCOM, the contestant with the next highest ranking in the average may be placed in that available position. (Non-notified TO's and VIR's after the turn out deadline will not be replaced). If the next highest ranked contestant is not available to accept the position, the next highest ranked contestant may be contacted and placed in that position. Replacement contestants competition order will be based on his ranking in the average (not on the ranking of the contestant he is replacing). This procedure will be followed until all positions are filled. In the riding events, if an animal has already been drawn for a contestant who has turned-out, the replacement contestant will draw an animal from a pool consisting of all animals that have been turned-out (includes DR's and VIR's).
TR - Only two loops allowed.
STALLS - Stalls can be reserved in advance by going to https://renorodeo.com/about/rodeo-grounds and following the link.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Contestant entry shall be at Gate 3.

PARKING - There will be no overnight trailer parking on the grounds. Secured off-site parking will be provided. Trailers will be allowed on the grounds for those contestants competing in that days event, then must be returned to the offsite parking.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes or a re-run is given for any other reason, the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into the herd.
TD, SW, TR - There will be one animal for every entry plus adequate extras.
TD - There will be a disqualification for a jerkdown as long as all criteria are in compliance with the jerkdown policy. Contestants will not be allowed to rope extras.

TD, SW, TR - If there are not enough contestants in the current year circuit money won category to fill the allotted circuit positions, the remaining positions will be filled with contestants from the previous year circuit money won category.
QUALIFICATIONS: BB, SB - 48 minimum entries. No compensation. Two go-rounds back to back, perf to perf, W/F's (12). $5000 held out for finals. No slack.
BR - 96 minimum entries. No compensation. W/F's (12). $5000 held out for finals. No slack.

TD, SW, TR - 96 minimum entries (or teams). Two go-rounds W/F's (12). Back to back, slack to perf, or slack to slack. First go-round will be at 10:00 AM each day (June 19-26). (Approximately 12 contestants or teams per day). The contestants with the top 8 fastest times from the first go-round will be placed in the performance (slowest time will run first, fastest time will run last). If splits result in more than 8, a random draw will determine which contestants will compete in the performance and which will compete in slack. The order of competition of ties from the first go-round will also be determined by random draw. If there are not 8 qualified times from the first go-round to fill the performance, the remaining positions will be filled by contestants based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions (Only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performance). The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in slack immediately following the completion of the first go-round in reverse order of their first go-round position. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order.
STK CONT.: Flying U Rodeo

GROUND RULES: Contestants who choose to enter the Legacy Steer Roping event must be at least 50 years old or a permit member at the time of entry closing. They must also be entered in the steer roping event at the Kadoka Buffalo Stampede Event. To be eligible, the contestant must not have been an NSFR qualifier during the past 3 years. Contestants will pay additional entry fees of $300. Contestants will not compete on any additional steers. The times that are recorded for the contestant's competition runs at the Kadoka Buffalo Stampede Event will be used to determine the pay-off. Pay-off will only include the entry fees for the contestants who entered the Legacy Steer Roping through PROCOM. 6% will be held out of the total amount for the PRCA prior to the pay-off. Only the three go-rounds and the average after three go-rounds will be included in the pay-off for the Legacy Steer Roping. There will be no additional added money and since no additional animals will be run, there will be no additional stock charge of PROCOM charge.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. detailLines: Ponoka AB CN
June 25 - July 1
Ponoka Stampede
ARENA: Ponoka Stampede Grounds
ADDRESS: 5616-39 Avenue
PERFS: 8 Perfs: June 25- 6:30 PM; June 26- 1:00 PM; June 27- 1:00 PM; June 28- 1:00 PM; June 29- 1:00 PM; June 30- 1:00 PM; July 1- 1:00 PM; July 1- 6:30 PM
SLACKS: June 25- 9:30 AM
EVENTS: BB SB BR @ $75000 TD SW @ $60000 TR-HD, TR-HL @ $60000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: BB-$250; SB-$200; TD-$500; SW-$500; TR-$500
PERMITS: BB SB BR
FINALS: July 1- 6:30 PM BB SB BR TD SW TR
GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANTS - May also enter online at www.rodeocanda.com between June 7 at 8 AM and June 8 at 2 PM.
ALL CONTESTANTS - A maximum of twelve (12) contestants will be drawn into the first (1st) performance at 6:30 PM on Monday June 25th.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Timed Event slack 9:30 am MST each morning.
PAYOUT - SW, TDR, TR payout will be 8 placings in go-rounds and aggregate. BB, SB, BR as per CPRA rulebook.
FORMAT: SB, BB, BR - 1 full go-round, with finals (12), top 4 showdown round.
TDR, SW, TR - 2 full go-rounds with finals (12), top 4 showdown.

TE - Timed Events first go-round run will be in the slack, each morning. Second go-round run will be in the afternoon performance, the same day. (ie., if a contestant is up in the first slack for his go-round run, he will be up in the first performance for his second go-round run). In the Timed Events in case of a foul/re-run, spare will be used.
TR - There will be a maximum of twelve (12) teams per performance. Both members of the team must be full members and/or Semi Pro.
Qualifications TDR & SW - Full & Semi Pro Members ONLY: Maximum 72 based on 75 CPRA/PRCA standings as of May 27, 2026.

Qualifications TR - Full & Semi Pro Members ONLY: Top 72 based off combined 75 CPRA/PRCA standings as of May 27, 2026. If more than 72 teams qualify from above then contestants with the least amount of money won from the 2025 season will be drawn out. If teams are drawn out, only teams that are both full members will remain entered.

Qualifications SB, BB, & BR - Full member, Semi Pro, and permits: Top 72 based on combined CPRA/PRCA standings as of May 27, 2026. If more than 72 contestants qualify from the above, then the contestants with the least amount of money won from the 2025 season, and up to and including May 27, 2026 will be drawn out.

TURN-OUT/ ALTERNATE PROCEDURE: If more than 72 entries contestants drawn out of the pool will be numbered as drawn out. (Ie: First drawn out will be number one, second drawn out will be number two etc.) This will be the order of alternate contestants. Contestants will be notified of there alternate position number at call back at which time they must provide their contact information to be eligible for re-entry. If or when a contestant turns-out the next alternate available will be contacted for re-entry.

MEDICAL EXEMPTION - Consideration will be given to those members who qualified in 2025 but because of injures were unable to compete at any rodeos after July 1, 2025. A letter on doctor's letterhead must be submitted to the CRES office prior to entries opening, this letter must detail the time frame in which contestant was unable to compete. Injury information must be given to CRES at the time of entry.
PLEASE NOTE - Section VII A. 1 & 3 and Section VIII A 13 of the CPRA rulebook will be strictly enforced by the Pro Rodeo Officials.
FINALS - $5,000 will be held out in each of the seven major events for the finals. Four (4) monies will be paid in the finals. Split 40-30-20-10.

TD, SW, TR - Top twelve (12), if a tie exists, it will be broken by the fastest time on any one head. If still tied, the tie will be broken by the second fastest time on any one head. If still tied the Canadian Standings as of June 18, 2025 will be the tie breaker.

SB, BB, BR - Top twelve (12), if a tie exists, it will be broken by going back to judge's card, the high mark contestant on the cowboy spur ride will break the tie. If still tied the Canadian Standings as of June 18, 2026 will be the tie breaker.

TURNING OUT FINALS - Contestants who turn-out of the Finals must notify the local Rodeo Office by Tuesday, June 30 no later than 6 PM MST. A $500 turn out fine will apply if the contestant fails to notify by the specified time. Contestants who are a notified turn-out or contestants who are unavailable at the start of the section of their event will be replaced by the next available contestant; next is defined by the 2026 Ponoka Stampede standings. Ponoka Stampede reserves the right to roll contestants into the Finals (to total of 12 contestants) in the event of turn outs. In case of ties between 13-14 etc., tie breaker rules to decide the next contestant into the finals, the procedure will be the same as determining the top twelve (12) qualifiers.

SHOWDOWN FORMAT - Cowboy Rule - Must make a qualified ride or run to be paid. NO GROUND MONEY WILL BE PAID. All monies paid in the SHOWDOWN will count towards CPRA/PRCA standings. In the event no qualified rides/times in the showdown there will no payout and the average winner will be the Stampede Champion. The Showdown prize money will be carried forward to the next year's Showdown, split with the same percentages as regular Showdown pay-out and will count for CPRA/PRCA standings. No times or score will be carried into the Showdown. All stock will be selected by the event reps and the committee. Order of competition will be fourth (4th) to first (1st), timed events must be split so as no back to back runs on the same horse. Top four (4) contestants, maximum of four (4), from the average of the rodeo will compete in the Showdown. If not enough qualified rides/runs for the Showdown, the highest score taken to the Finals will qualify (also includes injuries).
PRIZE MONEY - $15,000, held out per event for the Showdown split as follows:
Four (4) Qualified Rides/Runs:
Three (3) Qualified Rides/Runs:
Two (2) Qualified Rides/Runs:
One (1) Qualified Ride/Run:

TIE BREAKER FORMAT TO QUALIFY FOR SHOWDOWN - SB, BB, BR - Highest score on the Finals will break ties. If a tie still exists the contestant with the highest score in the first (1st) go-round will break the tie. If a tie still exists, the contestant with the most money won in previous go-rounds on two (2) head will advance. If a tie still exists, the highest marked spur ride on the judges' cards from the Finals (top 12) will proceed. If a tie till exists the Canadian Standings as of June 18, 2026 will be used.

TD, SW, TR - Fastest time in the Finals will break ties. If a ties still exists the fastest time in the first (1st) go-round will break the tie. If a tie still exists the contestant with the most money won in previous go-rounds on two (2) head will advance. If a tie still exists, the Canadian Standings as of June 18, 2026 will be used.

SHOWDOWN TIE BREAKERS - All tie breakers are based on qualified rides and times only. If a tie exists after the showdown contestants have competed once, there will be either a ride off or run off (depending on the event) between the tied contestants to determine the Champion. In rough stock events, if a ride off is required, any animals that were drawn as re-rides for the Finals and were not used will automatically be the ride-off animals. In timed events, if a run off is required, the designated spares will be used as the tie breaker animals. If a tie still exists after a ride off/run off, contestants will be co-champions.
STK CONT.: Wayne Vold Rodeo

detailLines: Salinas CA
July 16-19
California Rodeo Salinas
ARENA: Salinas Sports Complex
ADDRESS: 1034 N. Main Street
PERFS: 4 Perfs: July 16- 6:00 PM; July 17- 6:00 PM; July 18- 1:00 PM; July 19- 1:00 PM
SLACKS: July 16- 11:00 AM
EVENTS: BB SB BR TD SW @ $52500 TR-HD, TR-HL @ $52500
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: BB-$250; SB-$100; BR-$250+$100.00 DM; TD-$450; SW-$450; TR-$500
PERMITS:
FINALS: July 19- 1:00 PM BB SB BR TD SW TR
GROUND RULES: Only actual contestants and one companion allowed gate access.
ALL EVENTS: The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available position on Wed., July 8 between 9 AM and 11 AM. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
RIDING EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Tue., July 7 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.
TIMED EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Thurs., July 9 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.
ALL EVENTS - If contestant notifies a turnout prior to the 30-hour deadline for his competition time, turnout fines will be waived, if and only if he is replaced.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Secretary's office will be open from 12 noon to 4 PM on Weds. July 15.
ALL CONTESTANTS, STOCK CONTRACTORS, AND PERSONNEL - Must sign a release of liability with the secretary before participating.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Contestant parking will be open Monday, July 13 at 8 AM. No early entry.

ALL CONTESTANTS - If a contestant's actions are deemed detrimental to the PRCA, California Rodeo Salinas or the sport of rodeo in general, that contestant will not be eligible to compete at the California Rodeo Salinas in 2027.
RE - Any contestant who notifies a TO without a valid doctor's release or visible injury release will not be eligible to compete at the California Rodeo Salinas in 2026.
RE - Event representatives will have the opportunity to review the stock lists prior to the stock draw.
SLACK ORDER - Will be first go-round of LB, TD, SW, TR followed by second go-round of LB, TD, SW.

TE - If there are not enough contestants in the current year circuit money won category to fill the allotted circuit positions, the remaining positions will be filled with contestants from the previous year circuit money won category.

ALL CONTESTANTS WITH HORSES: All horses must be in compliance with current California Dept, of Food and Agriculture rules and requirements. Contestants who fail to comply with applicable health rules and requirements will be denied entry to the grounds or subject to removal from the grounds.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes (or a re-run is awarded for any other reason), the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into the herd.
TD - There will be a disqualification for a jerkdown as long as criteria are in compliance with the jerkdown policy.

ALL CONTESTANTS - If a contestant who qualifies for the finals notifies a turn-out, doctor's release or visible injury release through PROCOM, the contestant with the next highest ranking in the average may be contacted by PROCOM and placed in that available position. (Non-notified TO's and VIR's after the turn out deadline will not be replaced). If the next highest ranked contestant is not available to accept the position, the next highest ranked contestant may be contacted and placed in that position. This procedure will be followed until all positions are filled. The replacement contestants competition order will be based on his ranking in the average (not on the ranking of the contestant his is replacing). In the riding events, if an animal has already been drawn for a contestant who has turned-out, the replacement contestant will draw an animal from a pool consisting of all animals that have been turned-out (includes DR's and VIR's).
QUALIFICATIONS: BB & SB - 48 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. One go-round W/F's (12 plus splits to 14). $5,000 held out for finals. No slack.
BR - 75 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. One go-round W/F's (12 plus splits to 14). $5,000 held out for finals. There may be two sections during each performance. No slack.

TD - 90 minimum entries. Two go-rounds W/F's (12). Back to back, slack to slack, or slack to perf. Each day approximately 30 contestants will run their first go-round during slack. The top twelve fastest times from the first go-round each day will run their second go-round during the performance that day (slowest time will run first, fastest time will run last). If splits result in more than 12, a random draw will determine which contestants will compete in the performance (will not exceed 12) and which will compete in slack. The competition order of any ties from the first go-round will also be determined by random draw. If there are not 12 qualified times from the first go-round to fill the performance, the remaining positions will be filled based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions (only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performances). The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in that same slack (after the team roping) in reverse order of their first go-round positions. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order. Scorelines will be 25'. Contestants will compete from left side of roping chute.

SW - 80 minimum entries. Two go-rounds W/F's (12). Back to back, slack to slack, or slack to perf. Each day approximately 35 contestants will run their first go-round during slack Thursday and Friday, 20 Saturday. The top twelve fastest times from the first go-round each day will run their second go-round during the performance that day (slowest time will run first, fastest time will run last). If splits result in more than 12, a random draw will determine which contestants will compete in the performance (will not exceed 12) and which will compete in slack. The competition order of any ties from the first go-round will also be determined by random draw. If there are not 12 qualified times from the first go-round to fill the performance, the remaining positions will be filled based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions (only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performances). The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in that same slack (after the team toping) in reverse order of their first go-round positions. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order. Scorelines will be 25'. Contestants will compete from left side of roping chute.

TR - 120 minimum entries. Four go-rounds W/F's (12). Fifteen teams will run during the performance each day. The order of third and fourth go-round will be random draw. No trades allowed in the second and subsequent go-rounds. The entire fourth go-round will be run Sun, July 19 at 8 AM. Both contestants will compete from left side of roping chute. Cattle will be chute run (not drawn) if one head for every entry. Only two loops allowed per go-round. Scoreline will be 35'. Electric eye barrier will be used. Rule R3.1.1.1. and R3.3.6.1. will not be in effect.
STK CONT.: Corey & Lange Rodeo

fields.groundRules: May also enter online between 8 AM on June 24 and 2 PM on June 25 at www.rodeocanada.com.

detailLines: Regina SK CN
July 17-18
Pile O' Bones
ARENA: Brandt Center
ADDRESS: 1700 Elphinstone St.
PERFS: 2 Perfs: July 17- 7:00 PM; July 18- 7:00 PM
EVENTS: BB SB BR TD SW @ $9000 TR-HD, TR-HL @ $9000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: BB-$100; SB-$100; BR-$100; TD-$225; SW-$225; TR-$225
PERMITS: BB SB BR TD SW TR
GROUND RULES: May also enter online between 8 AM on June 24 and 2 PM on June 25 at www.rodeocanada.com.

SB, BB, BR - Maximum 30 contestants. If more than 30 contestants entered blended (top 50) CPRA/PRCA standing as of June 25, 2026 will be used to determine draw outs. If the qualifications are not filled by contestants within the top 50 blended standings will next go down the CPRA standings, followed by contestants with dollars won in 2026 PRCA standings, the remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of card holders, then semi-pro card holders with money won, then random draw of semi-pro card holders with no money won. If there are still open positions, all remaining openings will be filled by permits with money won followed by a random draw of permit holders with no money won.

SW, TDR, TR, LBR - Maximum of 75 contestants. If more than 60 contestants entered blended (top 75) CPRA/PRCA/WPRA standing as of Jun25, 2026 will be used to determine draw outs. If the qualifications are not filled by contestants within the top 75 blended standings will next go down the CPRA standings, followed by contestants with dollars won in 2026 PRCA standings, the remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of card holders, then semi-pro card holders with money won, then random draw of semi-pro card holders with no money won. If there are still open positions, all remaining openings will be filled by permits with money won followed by a random draw of permit holders with no money won.
Standardized Alternate Replacement Procedure will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 standardized ground rules.

Re-Entries: will be accepted for available positions in the roughstock at a time set by the CPRA after entries close to coincide with other entry schedules (typically all events for a particular weekend that require re-entries will be held on the same day) from 10am-12pm. See rodeo entry information on rodeo schedule. A contestant that re-enters will not be placed in a position that conflicts with his position at another CPRA rodeo or event. Additionally, if all spots are full on initial entry, a contestant that re-enters will be added to the alternate list (where accepted) but will be placed at the bottom of the list below those that entered on original entry day regardless of qualifications.
WALK-UP REPLACEMENTS: Walk up Replacement (implemented for 2026 season) will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 standardized ground rules.

* Any contestant that is a replacement will be responsible for entry fees. Any contestant that notifies a doctor release, visible release, vet release, draw out, or a notified turnout will still be responsible for any entry fees they would incur regardless if replaced or not. Doctor releases are not responsible for entry fees as an example.*
STK CONT.: C5 Rodeo

detailLines: Shakopee MN
July 17-19
Canterbury Park Rodeo
ARENA: Canterbury Park
ADDRESS: 1100 Canterbury Road
PERFS: 3 Perfs: July 17- 7:00 PM; July 18- 7:00 PM; July 19- 5:00 PM
EVENTS: BB SB BR @ $8000 TD SW @ $4000 TR-HD, TR-HL @ $4000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES:
PERMITS: BB SB BR SW
GROUND RULES: CO-APPROVED WITH THE BADLANDS CIRCUIT.
ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
ALL EVENTS - The "walk-up replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions on Mon., July 13 between 9 AM and 12 PM. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
TRADE DEADLINE - Fri., July 10 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.

CONTESTANTS WITH HORSES - All horses (including pony/outrider horses) entering the grounds for the first time must have an original health certificate (Certificate of Veterinary Inspection) issued within five (5) days of their arrival and a negative Coggins Test Certificate issued within twelve (12) months of arrival. Equine rhinopneumonitis (EHV-1 and EHV-4) and Influenza vaccination dates, specific product used, and expiration date and rectal temperatures for each horse should be included on the health certificate.

VACCINATIONS: Every horse entering the enclosure of the racetrack must have been vaccinated by a veterinarian with an FDA approved modified live or killed virus vaccine specific for EHV-1 and EHV-4 and Influenza not less than 14 days and not more than 180 days prior to date of entry. The specific product used and expiration date as well as the date the horse was vaccinated must appear on the health certificate. Horses must be vaccinated no later than July 3, 2026.

ALL OTHER ANIMALS: All other animals will require a health certificate. No specific requirement on those but event hired veterinarian should know the information needed. Those should be completed by July 3, 2026. All health certificates with vaccination information and a negative Coggins test certificate must be submitted to Andrew Vold no later than July 16, 2026. Certificates can be submitted via email or photos of documents can be sent via text to the information. Andrew Vold at avold@canterburypark.com, 763-234-5966 (cell phone).
QUALIFICATIONS: BB, SB, BR - 36 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack.
STK CONT.: Dakota Rodeo
